body.text: prathamaṃ prāmāṇika ācāryaḥ śiṣye prasāda-sampratyayābhilāṣātmikāṃ śraddhāṃ janayet / tato bodhicittānuśaṃsām uktvā utsāhaṃ janayet / tataḥ paraṃ viśiṣṭavihāre viśiṣṭapūjopakaraṇaṃ sthāpayet / āryasaṃghān āmantrya, praṇamya, pādau prakṣālya, āsanaṃ pradāya, uttarānuttarapūjopakaraṇaiḥ sampūjya pūjāmeghamantrānapi triruccaret /
body.translated_text: First, the authoritative <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) should generate in the student <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) consisting of serene confidence, trust, and aspiration. Then, having spoken of the benefits of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), he should generate enthusiasm. Thereafter, in a distinguished <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), he should arrange distinguished worship materials. Having invited the noble <s>Saṅgha</s>, having bowed, having washed their feet, having offered seats, and having worshipped with supreme and unsurpassed worship materials, he should also recite the <s>Pūjāmegha</s> (Cloud of Offerings) mantras three times.

body.text: stotā sugataviśiṣṭaguṇasmaraṇadvārā sādaraṃ stutvā tattadvṛddhikarāṇyapi padāni uccaret / tataśca deśanā-anumodanā-adhyeṣaṇā-prārthanā-pariṇāmanādayaḥ karaṇīyāḥ / tataḥ śraddhāvān śiṣya ācārya praṇamet / adhyeṣaṇādibhirdvividhaṃ bodhicittaṃ samutpādya teṣāṃ svasvabhāvaṃ bhedaṃ vaiśiṣṭyañcāpi khyāpayet /
body.translated_text: The praiser, having praised with reverence through recollection of the distinguished qualities of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), should also recite verses that promote the growth of those qualities. Then, <s>deśanā</s> (teaching), <s>anumodanā</s> (rejoicing), <s>adhyeṣaṇā</s> (requesting), <s>prārthanā</s> (prayer), <s>pariṇāmanā</s> (dedication), and so forth should be performed. Then the faithful student should bow to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher). Having generated the twofold <s>bodhicitta</s> through entreaties and so forth, he should also make known their own nature, distinctions, and special characteristics.

body.text: tataḥ bodhicaryā (ṇāṃ_) ṣaṭpāramitānāṃ, catuḥsaṃgrahavastūnāṃ caturapramāṇādīnāṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ, hetuṃ, phalaṃ, śikṣākramaṃ, cyutyacyutidoṣaguṇān yathāvidhiśikṣādikamapi vistareṇa nirdiśet / sā ca apramādena samprajanyena smṛtyā ca grahaṇīyeti śikṣeta /
body.translated_text: Then he should explain in detail the characteristics, causes, fruits, order of training, faults and virtues of falling and not falling, and the training according to the proper rules regarding the <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening), the <s>ṣaṭpāramitās</s> (six perfections), the <s>catuḥsaṃgrahavastūni</s> (four means of gathering disciples), the <s>caturapramāṇas</s> (four immeasurables), and so forth. And he should train the student that these are to be grasped with <s>apramāda</s> (diligence), <s>samprajanya</s> (clear comprehension), and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness).

body.text: teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kramaṃ cyutyacyutidoṣaguṇādīnapi śikṣeta / tadanuṣṭhānāyāpi tīvravīryamutpādya nidhyānaduḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntim avikṣipta-samādhiṃ prajñāniḥsvabhāvatāṃ ca jñātvā triśikṣāṃ trividhaprajñāṃ vā samādhāya caryāpathavidhinā śikṣeta iti nirdiśet / ante praṇidhānena parisamāpayed ityapi vadet /
body.translated_text: He should also train in their characteristics, order, and the faults and virtues of falling and not falling. He should instruct that, for the practice thereof, having generated intense <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), knowing the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) of enduring the suffering of contemplation, undistracted <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and the essencelessness understood through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), one should train according to the method of conduct by establishing oneself in the <s>triśikṣā</s> (three trainings) or the threefold <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). He should also say that at the end, one should conclude with <s>praṇidhāna</s> (aspirational prayers).

body.text: ayaṃ hi ācāryadeśanākriyākramaḥ / śiṣyo 'pi yathāvidhirupadiṣṭaḥ tathā śikṣeta / ayaṃ tu lākṣaṇikamahāyānacittotpāda-śikṣā-deśanā-vidhiḥ kramo vā audārikatayā darśitaḥ / vistareṇa tu parato jñātavyam /
body.translated_text: This indeed is the procedure for the <s>ācārya's</s> (teacher's) instructional practice. The student also should train just as has been instructed according to the proper method. This procedure or method for the teaching and training of the characteristic <s>Mahāyāna</s> generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) has been shown in a general manner. The details, however, should be known from other sources.
The Concise Procedure of Guru Practices (<s>Saṃkṣipta-guru-kriyā-kramaḥ</s>), composed by the great <s>paṇḍita</s> and <s>ācārya</s> <s>Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna</s>, is completed.
